text.p: Germany's Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel Bank AG on Thursday reported a 9.9 percent rise in its nine-month operating profits, boosted by steady growth in both net and commission income.
However the bank's 808.1 million marks ($537.3 million) in operating earnings after provisions was well below analysts' forecasts, which had ranged from 910 million to 920 million marks.
Hypo-Bank said in a mandatory statement that its risk provisions in the period had risen 20 percent to 961 million marks. Operating income before provisions rose 15.2 percent to 1.77 billion marks.
Net income from own-account trading rose 6.5 percent to 130.0 million marks.
The bank, the last of Germany's Big Five commercial banks to report nine-month earnings, is to give more details at a news conference later on Thursday.
Hypo-Bank also said it planned to raise its stake in British asset management group Foreign & Colonial Management Limited to 65 percent from the 50 percent stake it has held since 1989.
The move would allow it to consolidate the British firm into its group accounts, leading to extra commission income of 150-170 million marks, Hypo-Bank said.
